name: Overfilled or badly loaded paper tray
summary: Too much paper, or paper not sitting flat and square, makes the rollers grab badly and causes jams.
steps: Switch off the printer and remove all paper from the tray.
Fan the paper stack and tap it flat on a table so the edges line up.
Reload below the maximum fill mark.
Slide the paper guides until they lightly touch the stack.
Switch on and print one test page.

name: Torn paper or foreign object in the paper path
summary: A scrap of paper, staple or label is blocking the paper path or a sensor, so the printer reports a jam.
steps: Switch off and unplug the printer.
Open every cover and the rear access door.
Pull any stuck sheet out slowly in the direction the paper normally travels, to avoid tearing it.
Shine a torch along the paper path and remove every small scrap.
Close all covers, plug in, switch on and print a test page.

name: Worn or dirty pickup roller
summary: The rubber roller that pulls paper from the tray is dirty with dust or has worn smooth.
steps: Switch off and unplug the printer.
Open the paper path and find the pickup roller.
Wipe it gently with a lint-free cloth lightly dampened with water, then let it dry fully.
Reload fresh paper and try again.
If it still will not pick up paper, the roller needs replacing: see a technician.

name: Damp, curled or unsuitable paper
summary: Humid or curled paper sticks together, jams, smudges ink and misfeeds.
steps: Remove the paper from the tray.
Replace it with fresh dry paper from a sealed ream of the correct weight, usually 75 to 80 grams.
Store paper flat and sealed, away from damp.
Set the correct paper type in the print settings.

name: Toner running low
summary: The laser toner cartridge is nearly empty, so the print becomes pale or streaky.
steps: Switch off the printer and open the cartridge cover.
Remove the toner cartridge carefully.
Rock it gently side to side five or six times to redistribute the toner.
Reinstall it firmly and close the cover.
If print is still faded, replace the toner cartridge.

name: Clogged print head nozzles or low ink
summary: Dried ink blocks the nozzles of an inkjet print head, giving faded print, streaks, missing colours or blank pages.
steps: Check the ink levels in the printer software.
Run the print head cleaning utility from the printer software or control panel.
Print a nozzle check pattern to see whether the lines are complete.
Repeat cleaning at most two or three times because each cleaning uses ink.
If it is still poor, replace the cartridge or leave the printer switched on overnight and try again.

name: Damaged drum or dirty laser components
summary: A scratched drum, dirty cleaning blade or leaking cartridge causes lines and streaks on laser printouts.
steps: Switch off and let the printer cool.
Remove the cartridge and look for scratches, toner leaks or dirt.
Wipe the inside of the printer with a dry lint-free cloth. Never touch the green drum surface.
Reinstall the cartridge and print a test page.
If streaks remain, replace the cartridge or imaging drum.

name: Worn drum or imaging unit
summary: The photosensitive drum is worn or damaged, causing marks that repeat at the same spacing and ghost images.
steps: Measure the distance between the repeating marks.
Compare it with the drum circumference in the printer manual, or just replace the drum.
Replace the imaging unit or drum with a correct model.
Reset the drum counter if the printer requires it.
Print a test page.

name: Failing fuser unit
summary: The fuser does not heat or press correctly, so toner is not bonded to the paper. Print rubs off, pages wrinkle or ghost images appear.
steps: Switch off the printer and wait at least 30 minutes. The fuser gets very hot.
Do not touch the fuser area.
Check that the correct paper type is selected in the settings.
If the problem continues, the fuser unit must be replaced: take it to a technician.

name: Cartridge seal not removed or cartridge not seated
summary: A new laser cartridge still has its protective seal, or is not clicked fully into place, so nothing prints.
steps: Switch off and open the cartridge cover.
Remove the cartridge and check for a plastic seal or orange tape. Pull it out fully.
Remove any protective cover from the cartridge contacts.
Insert the cartridge until it clicks into place.
Close the cover and print a test page.

name: Empty ink cartridge or tank
summary: The ink has run out, so the page prints blank or with missing colours.
steps: Check the ink levels in the printer software.
Replace the empty cartridge or refill the tank with the correct ink.
Run a print head cleaning once.
Print a nozzle check page to confirm.

name: Printer set to offline or not the default printer
summary: The computer is holding jobs because the printer is marked offline or the wrong printer is selected.
steps: Make sure the printer is on, ready and has no error on its display.
On the computer open Printers and Scanners and select your printer.
Open the print queue and make sure Use Printer Offline is not ticked.
Set this printer as the default.
Restart the printer and the computer, then print a test page.

name: Faulty USB cable or port
summary: A damaged, long or loose USB cable, or a bad port or hub, interrupts the connection.
steps: Switch off the printer and unplug the USB cable at both ends.
Use a different, shorter cable, ideally no longer than three metres.
Plug it straight into a port on the computer, not into a hub.
Switch the printer on and wait for the computer to detect it.
Print a test page.

name: Weak Wi-Fi signal or changed network settings
summary: The printer lost its network or its address changed after a router restart or password change.
steps: Move the printer closer to the router.
Restart the router and then the printer.
Reconnect the printer to Wi-Fi from its control panel and enter the current password.
Print a network configuration page to see the printer address.
If the address changed, remove and re-add the printer on the computer, or reserve a fixed address for it in the router.

name: Stuck print spooler or queue
summary: A bad or large job is blocking the Windows print queue so nothing else prints.
steps: Open the print queue and cancel all documents.
Press the Windows key, type Services, and open it.
Find Print Spooler, right-click it and choose Restart.
If jobs still will not clear, stop the service, delete the files inside the spool PRINTERS folder, then start the service again.
Print a test page.

name: Missing, outdated or corrupt printer driver
summary: The driver software that lets the computer talk to the printer is missing or damaged, often after an update.
steps: Remove the printer from Printers and Scanners.
Uninstall the old printer driver and software from the Apps list.
Download the latest driver for your exact model from the manufacturer website, using an internet connection on the computer.
Install it, restart the computer and reconnect the printer.
Print a test page.

name: Cartridge chip not recognised or incompatible cartridge
summary: The printer cannot read the cartridge chip because of dirty contacts, a wrong model, or a non-original cartridge.
steps: Switch off the printer and remove the cartridge.
Wipe the metal contacts on the cartridge and in the printer with a dry lint-free cloth.
Check that the cartridge number matches your printer model.
Reinstall firmly until it clicks.
If it is a refilled or clone cartridge and still fails, try an original cartridge.

name: Power supply or power board fault
summary: The printer receives no usable power, even from a good socket and cable.
steps: Plug the printer directly into a wall socket, not an extension, and try a different cable if it is removable.
Unplug the printer, hold the power button for 30 seconds, plug it back in and try again.
If there is still no sign of life, do not open the printer. The power supply needs a technician.

name: Worn gears or mechanical fault
summary: Worn or broken gears or a failing motor cause grinding or clicking.
steps: Switch off the printer immediately.
Check for a jam or a loose item and remove it gently. Do not force anything.
Switch on again and listen. If the noise returns, stop using it.
Take the printer to a technician for gear or motor replacement.

name: Overheating or electrical hazard
summary: A burning smell, smoke or extreme heat can mean a short circuit or a failing fuser. This is a safety risk.
steps: Switch off the printer and unplug it from the wall straight away if it is safe to do so.
Do not open the printer or touch internal parts. Let it cool.
Open a window to ventilate the room.
Do not use the printer again until a qualified technician has checked it.

name: Print head carriage obstruction
summary: Packing tape, a jammed sheet or debris stops the print head carriage from moving.
steps: Switch off the printer and unplug it.
Open the cover and remove packing tape, paper or other obstructions.
With the power off, gently slide the carriage by hand to check it moves freely.
Plug in, switch on and let the printer initialise.
If it still sticks, take it to a technician.

name: Wrong print settings
summary: Draft mode, greyscale mode or the wrong paper type setting gives poor quality, smudges or missing colours.
steps: Open the print settings in your application.
Set the quality to Normal or Best, not Draft or Economy.
Make sure colour printing is selected, not greyscale or black only.
Choose the correct paper type, for example plain or glossy.
Print a test page.

name: Wrong driver language or corrupt print data
summary: A mismatched driver or corrupt job sends data the printer cannot interpret, so it prints strange characters.
steps: Cancel the job and switch the printer off and on.
Try printing a different document from a different application.
Reinstall the correct driver for your exact model.
Update the printer firmware if the manufacturer provides an update.

name: Worn separation pad
summary: The pad that separates sheets has worn smooth, so several sheets are pulled in together.
steps: Remove the paper and fan the sheets so they do not stick together.
Clean the separation pad with a lint-free cloth lightly dampened with water.
Reload less paper and try again.
If it still multi-feeds, the pad needs replacing: see a technician.

name: Paper guides not adjusted
summary: Loose paper guides let the stack slide sideways so pages are fed at an angle.
steps: Remove the paper from the tray.
Square the stack on a table.
Reload it and slide the guides in until they gently touch the edges.
Print a test page and check the alignment.

name: Slow printing from settings or network
summary: High-quality settings, huge image files or a weak wireless link make printing slow.
steps: Set print quality to Normal instead of Best or High.
Reduce very large images in the document.
If you are on Wi-Fi, move closer to the router or switch to a USB cable to compare.
Close other programs, then update the printer driver.

name: High-voltage power supply or corona fault
summary: A fault in the laser printer's high-voltage section can make the whole page come out black.
steps: Switch off the printer.
Remove and reseat the toner cartridge to rule out a poor contact.
If the pages are still black, stop printing to avoid wasting toner and paper.
Take the printer to a technician.

name: General error state needing a reset
summary: The printer shows an error light or code that has no more specific cause yet.
steps: Check the display or light pattern and note any error code.
Open all covers and check for jams and a seated cartridge.
Switch off, unplug for 60 seconds, plug in and switch on again.
Look up any error code in the manual for your exact model.
If the error returns, take the printer to a technician.

name: Worn-out dot matrix ribbon
summary: A dot matrix printer prints by striking an inked ribbon. When the ink in the ribbon is used up, print becomes faint or disappears.
steps: Switch off the printer and open the printer cover.
Take out the old ribbon cartridge.
Fit a new ribbon cartridge made for your printer model.
Turn the ribbon tightening knob in the direction of the arrow to remove any slack.
Close the cover, switch on and print a self test page.

name: Damaged dot matrix print head pin
summary: When a whole line of dots is missing from every character, one or more pins in the print head are usually broken. The manufacturer advises having the head replaced, not doing it yourself.
steps: Stop printing, because carrying on can damage the head further.
First rule out the ribbon: reseat the ribbon cartridge and take up any slack.
Print a self test page as described in your printer's manual.
If the same line is still missing through every letter, a print head pin is broken.
Do not replace the print head yourself. Contact a dealer or qualified technician.

name: Loose, twisted or badly seated ribbon
summary: If the ribbon is slack, twisted or not clipped in, the pins strike paper without ink, so dots or whole characters go missing.
steps: Switch off the printer and open the cover.
Take the ribbon cartridge out and check the ribbon is not twisted.
Refit it so it clicks into place and the ribbon passes between the print head and its guide.
Turn the tightening knob to remove slack.
Close the cover and print a self test page.

name: Continuous paper not fed correctly by the tractor
summary: Continuous paper must sit on both tractor sprockets with the paper release lever in the continuous position. Misaligned holes or an obstructed paper supply make it skew, tear or jam.
steps: Switch off the printer before moving the paper release lever.
Set the paper release lever to the continuous paper position.
Fit the holes on both sides of the paper onto the sprockets so they line up, then lock the sprocket units and close their covers.
Keep the paper supply within one metre of the printer, with nothing blocking it.
Check the paper is a size and thickness your printer supports, then switch on and print a test.

name: Thermal paper roll loaded the wrong way
summary: Thermal paper has a heat-sensitive coating on one side only. If the roll is put in backwards, the head heats the plain side and the receipt comes out blank.
steps: Switch off the printer and open the roll paper cover.
Take out the roll and turn it around so the paper comes off the roll as shown in the diagram inside the cover.
Pull out a little paper so there is no slack, then close the cover.
Hold the Feed button while switching on to print a self test.
If the test is still blank, check that the paper really is thermal paper.

name: Non-thermal paper in a thermal printer
summary: A thermal printer has no ink. It only prints on heat-sensitive thermal paper, so ordinary paper rolls always come out blank.
steps: Scratch the paper quickly with a fingernail. Thermal paper shows a dark mark, plain paper does not.
Buy thermal paper rolls of the right width for your printer.
Fit the new roll the correct way round and close the cover.
Print a self test page to confirm.

name: Dirty thermal print head
summary: Paper dust and residue build up on the thermal head, so receipts print faint or with pale bands. The manufacturer recommends cleaning about every three months.
steps: Switch off the printer and let it cool. The head can be very hot after printing.
Open the roll paper cover.
Gently wipe the thermal head with a cotton bud dampened with isopropyl alcohol.
Clean the rubber platen roller the same way to remove paper dust.
Wait until everything is completely dry, then close the cover and print a test.

name: Receipt paper cover open or paper roll finished
summary: Thermal receipt printers stop and light the error or paper LED when the roll cover is not fully closed or the roll has run out.
steps: Press the roll paper cover down firmly until it clicks shut.
Open the cover and check there is paper left on the roll. Replace the roll if it is finished.
Pull out a little paper and close the cover again.
If the error light stays on, switch off, wait ten seconds and switch on.
If the error light still comes back, contact a qualified service person.

name: Receipt auto-cutter jam
summary: A scrap of paper or a foreign object caught in the auto-cutter stops the blade and makes the printer report a cutter error.
steps: Switch off the printer and let the head cool.
Open the roll paper cover.
Remove any jammed paper or object near the cutter. Do not pull hard and do not touch the thermal head.
Refit the roll, close the cover and switch on.
If the cutter error keeps returning, have a technician check the cutter.

name: Waste ink pads full
summary: Inkjet printers collect ink from cleaning cycles in absorbent pads. When an internal counter says the pads are full, the printer stops to prevent ink leaking. Canon shows code 5B00 and Epson shows a service life message.
steps: Write down the exact message or code on the screen.
Switch off, unplug for ten minutes, then try again in case it was a false alarm.
If the message names a maintenance box, that box is user-replaceable. Fit a new one.
Otherwise the pads are inside the printer. Contact an authorised service centre or certified technician.
Avoid counter reset tools from unofficial websites. They can damage the printer or let ink leak.

name: Inkjet print head failure
summary: A print head error, such as Canon code B200, often follows printing with an empty cartridge, which overheats the nozzles. It can also be a head or main board fault.
steps: Switch off and unplug the printer for ten to fifteen minutes, then switch on.
Open the cover and push each cartridge down until it clicks.
Clean the copper contacts on the cartridges with a lint-free cloth lightly dampened with distilled water, then let them dry.
Switch on and try again. Do not pull cables to free the carriage.
If the error stays, the print head or board needs a qualified technician.

name: Drum counter not reset after fitting a new drum
summary: Some laser printers count pages on the drum. After a new drum is fitted the counter must be reset, or the Replace Drum message stays on. Resetting does not fix an old drum.
steps: Make sure a new drum unit really is installed.
Open the front cover with the printer switched on.
Follow your model's drum counter reset, for example on many Brother models press Clear or Options, then 1 or the Up arrow.
Close the cover when the display says Accepted.
If the message stays, remove the drum and toner, unplug for ten minutes, refit them and try again.

name: Dirty corona wire on the drum unit
summary: On many Brother laser printers the Drum ! message means the corona wire inside the drum unit needs cleaning. A dirty wire also causes streaks and patchy print.
steps: Open the front cover.
Take out the toner cartridge and drum unit together.
Gently slide the green tab on the drum unit from left to right and back several times.
Return the tab to its home position so its arrow lines up with the arrow on the drum. If not, pages get a vertical stripe.
Put the toner and drum back, close the cover and print a test. If the message stays, the drum unit needs replacing.

name: Paper size or type does not match the settings
summary: The paper size or type chosen on the computer does not match the paper in the tray or the tray setting, so the printer stops and asks for different paper.
steps: Check which paper size the document uses, for example A4 or Letter.
Load that size of paper in the tray and slide the guides against it.
Set the same paper size and type for the tray on the printer's menu.
Make the same choice in the print settings on the computer.
Press Go or OK on the printer, or print again.

name: Fuser heating error
summary: The fuser must heat up within a set time. If it does not, laser printers report a fuser error, such as HP error 50 or Canon E000. It can also be caused by a poor power supply.
steps: Switch the printer off and wait at least fifteen minutes for the fuser to cool.
Plug the printer straight into a wall socket, not a UPS, stabiliser or extension strip.
Switch on and leave it idle for fifteen minutes.
If the error clears, keep it on the direct wall socket.
If it comes back, the fuser or power board needs a qualified technician.

name: Print job the printer cannot process
summary: A corrupt or very large print job, or old printer firmware, can make laser printers stop with a 49 service error or an out of memory message.
steps: Cancel all print jobs on every computer that uses this printer.
Switch the printer off, unplug the network or USB cable, and switch it on again.
If it now reaches Ready, the problem was a bad print job. Reconnect and print something simple.
For a large document, lower the print resolution or print fewer pages at a time.
If the error keeps returning, update the printer firmware from the manufacturer's website or call a technician.

name: Waste toner container full
summary: Many office laser printers and photocopiers, such as Kyocera, Ricoh, Konica and Xerox models, collect used toner in a waste box. When it is full, the machine stops printing.
steps: Check the display or status page for the waste toner box part number.
Open the cover shown in your manual and remove the full waste toner box carefully, keeping it upright.
Seal it in a bag so toner does not spill.
Fit a new waste toner box and close the cover.
If the message stays with a new box, have a technician check the sensor.

name: Label printer media sensor not calibrated
summary: Label printers find the gap between labels with a sensor. After loading a new label size the sensor must be calibrated, or labels skip, print across the gap, or show media out.
steps: Open the printer and check the labels pass under the movable media sensor.
Slide the sensor so it sits under the gap or black mark, not at the edge of the labels.
Close the printer and run a media calibration. On many Zebra desktop models, hold Feed until the light flashes twice, then let go.
Wipe the sensor with a dry cloth or air duster if calibration fails, then calibrate again.
Print a test label.

name: Label media or ribbon loaded wrongly
summary: Labels print nothing if the printable side faces away from the head, if thermal transfer labels are used without a ribbon, or if the ribbon is finished or loaded with the ink side facing the wrong way.
steps: Check the printable side of the labels faces up towards the print head.
Find out if your labels are direct thermal, which need no ribbon, or thermal transfer, which need a ribbon.
If a ribbon is needed, fit it so its ink side faces the labels, and replace it if it is finished.
Close the printer and press Feed once to line up the labels.
Print a test label.

name: Label print too light: darkness setting or dirty head
summary: Faint labels usually come from a darkness setting that is too low, a print speed that is too fast, or a dirty print head.
steps: Print the printer's print quality or configuration label to see the current darkness and speed.
Increase the darkness setting a little or lower the print speed.
Switch off and let the print head cool.
Clean the print head with a cleaning pen or a cotton bud with isopropyl alcohol, and let it dry.
Print a test label.

name: Air in the ink tubes after refilling
summary: On ink tank printers such as Epson EcoTank, Canon G series and HP Smart Tank, letting a tank run dry lets air into the tubes. After refilling, pages may print blank, faint or with gaps until ink is drawn back through.
steps: Check each ink tank is at least one third full.
Print a nozzle check pattern to see which colours are missing.
Run a head cleaning, or the stronger Power Cleaning or ink flush from the printer menu or utility.
Print another nozzle check. If it is still poor, switch off and wait at least twelve hours before another Power Cleaning.
If several cleanings do not help, contact the manufacturer's service centre.

name: Cover or door not fully closed
summary: Office printers will not print while a front, back or fuser cover is open or not latched.
steps: Open the front cover and close it firmly until it clicks.
Do the same for the back cover and any fuser cover inside it.
Check nothing such as paper or a toner cartridge is stopping a cover from closing.
If the message stays, switch off and on again.

name: Phone cannot find or print to the printer
summary: Android phones print through the Default Print Service or Mopria, and iPhones through AirPrint. The phone and printer must be on the same network and the print service must be switched on.
steps: After switching the printer on, wait two or three minutes for it to join the network.
Connect the phone to the same Wi-Fi network as the printer, not a guest network.
On Android, open Settings, Connected devices, Printing, and switch on Default Print Service or Mopria Print Service.
Update the phone's software and the printer's firmware.
If it still cannot see the printer, connect the phone directly with Wi-Fi Direct.

name: Machine reports a service call code
summary: Office copiers and printers, such as Ricoh, show an SC or service call code when they detect a hardware, temperature or control fault that needs a technician.
steps: Write down the exact code and the machine model.
Switch the machine off, wait one minute and switch it on once.
If the code comes back, do not keep switching it off and on, especially for heat or fuser codes.
Call an authorised service technician and give them the code.

name: Extra blank pages from the document or settings
summary: Extra blank pages usually come from empty pages or page breaks in the document, a paper size that does not match the tray, a separator page setting, or two sheets feeding together.
steps: Open print preview and check whether the document itself has empty pages or extra page breaks.
Make sure the paper size in the print settings matches the paper in the tray.
In the printer properties, switch off any separator or banner page.
Fan the paper before loading so sheets do not stick together.
Print the document again.

name: Two-sided printing disabled or blocked
summary: Automatic two-sided printing stops if the back cover or two-sided tray is not fully closed, if the paper size is not supported for two-sided printing, or if it is switched off in the print settings.
steps: Close the back cover of the printer until it locks.
If your printer has a two-sided tray, push it firmly into place.
Use a paper size your printer supports for two-sided printing, usually A4 or Letter.
In the print settings, choose two-sided or duplex printing.
Print again.
